You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`

> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the entity was taken private and
> deregistered, there is no post-closing public 10-K; the traceable realized record is
> limited to the deregistration filing, EDGAR filer searches, and reputable secondary
> reporting. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was
> structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- On February 16, 2018, Buffalo Wild Wings, Inc. filed a Form 15-12G certifying
  termination of registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) of the Exchange
  Act and suspension of its duty to file reports under Sections 13(a)/15(d); the filing
  recorded "One" approximate holder of record as of the certification date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001062449-18-000026, Form 15-12G]
- A search of Buffalo Wild Wings, Inc.'s (CIK 0001062449) EDGAR filing history for
  annual reports finds no Form 10-K filed after the pre-merger fiscal-2016 10-K (filed
  2017-02-17); no periodic report covering fiscal years within the ~2021-2023 outcome
  window was located under this CIK. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001062449&type=10-K]
- Contemporaneous reputable press reported that, upon completing the acquisition on
  February 5, 2018, "Arby's Restaurant Group Inc. completed a $2.9 billion acquisition
  of Buffalo Wild Wings Inc. and renamed itself Inspire Brands Inc.," with Buffalo Wild
  Wings continuing as one of several distinct brands under the renamed private parent.
  [SRC: https://www.nrn.com/mergers-acquisitions/arby-s-buffalo-wild-wings-new-parent-inspire-brands-debuts]
- An EDGAR company-name search for annual-report (Form 10-K) filers under "Inspire
  Brands," "Arby's Restaurant Group," "Buffalo Wild Wings International," and "IRB
  Holding" returned no matching SEC-registered filer; no periodic report specifically
  disclosing the acquired Buffalo Wild Wings business's post-close trajectory was
  located under any of these names. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&company=Inspire+Brands&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40&output=atom]
- Beyond the ~2021-2023 window: reputable press reported that Inspire Brands submitted
  a confidential draft registration statement to the SEC in connection with a proposed
  initial public offering, reported May 8, 2026; the reporting names Buffalo Wild Wings
  among the operating brands but discloses no Buffalo-Wild-Wings-specific financial
  figures. [SRC: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/inspire-brands-files-for-initial-public-offering-with-sec-432SI-4673899]

## Realized record within the outcome window (secondary/press-sourced)
- A legal-news tracking source reports a September 7, 2021 case alleging California
  Buffalo Wild Wings employees were "owed unpaid wages for off-the-clock work"; a
  November 18, 2021 class action claiming the company "charges hidden delivery fee
  disguised as 'service fee'"; and an August 31, 2022 class action alleging the company
  was "hit with class action over 'hidden' carryout fee." [SRC: https://www.classaction.org/news/category/buffalo-wild-wings-inc]
- The same source reports a March 10, 2023 class action alleging Buffalo Wild Wings
  "boneless wings are falsely advertised" (i.e., not bone-in wing meat). [SRC: https://www.classaction.org/news/category/buffalo-wild-wings-inc]
- No source was found in which Inspire Brands (or any successor entity) separately
  discloses audited revenue, net income, impairment, or comparable financial-scalar
  figures specifically for the Buffalo Wild Wings business for fiscal years within the
  ~2021-2023 window. [UNVERIFIED]

## Items sought but not found
- No SEC filing, press release, or reputable-press report was located describing a
  bankruptcy, dissolution, or divestiture of the Buffalo Wild Wings business within the
  ~2021-2023 window. [UNVERIFIED]
- No source was found reconciling a precise, internally-consistent system-wide
  restaurant unit count or closure count for Buffalo Wild Wings specifically within the
  ~2021-2023 fiscal years from a single verifiable table; figures encountered in
  secondary trade reporting for this period were not stable enough across sources to
  cite as an outcome scalar here. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because Buffalo Wild Wings, Inc. was taken private and deregistered (Form 15-12G,
  February 16, 2018), there is no public audited outcome record (10-K) for the
  ~2021-2023 window, and no successor entity (the renamed private parent or any
  affiliated holding company) was found to be an SEC periodic-report filer during that
  window. [SRC: SEC accession 0001062449-18-000026, Form 15-12G]
- The only traceable realized-record facts within the fixed window are a recurring
  pattern of consumer/employment class-action filings against the Buffalo Wild Wings
  entity (2021-2023, fee-disclosure and wage claims, plus a 2023 product-labeling
  claim); no audited financial scalar or divestiture/bankruptcy event was located for
  the business in this period. [SRC: https://www.classaction.org/news/category/buffalo-wild-wings-inc]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the financial-
  scalar outcome: the absence of a public periodic-reporting record for the acquired
  business (or its private parent) precludes a sourced determination of its realized
  3-5-year financial trajectory.

[SLICE END]
